report:
Short answer
- The evidence supports a consistent, interpretable difference: checkpoint B (the “plus” vector) pushes residual activations toward vocabulary about small commercial/consumer domains — chiefly cooking/restaurant/baking terminology and a separate cluster of health/academic/occupation-ish tokens (e.g. chiropractic, dissertation, doctoral, cadmium, billionaire, multinational, Obama/Michele).  
- The effect is concentrated at very early token positions (pos0–pos2) and especially at pos1 in later layers (layers ~16–25), so it will strongly affect the model’s next-token predictions early in a sequence.  
- I cannot say a more specific training objective (e.g. “promote ads” vs “promote health quackery”) is definitely the cause; the data support a domain/topic shift but do not prove a single named objective.

Why I conclude this
- Localization: the L2-norm map shows the difference is tiny in very early layers then grows, peaking at early token positions in middle-to-late layers (huge values at layers ~16–25, especially pos1). That pattern indicates the difference mainly alters the model’s early next-token logits (not only deep contextual features).  
- Logit-lens tokens: the highest-norm cells point repeatedly at a small set of semantic clusters rather than random tokens. One clear cluster is food/restaurant/cooking/baking: tokens like restaurant, Restaurant, Cooking, cooking, Chef, kitchen, baking, Cake, Cook, microwave, Baked, Cheesecake, etc. Another recurring cluster is health/academic/occupation/finance-ish tokens: chiropractic, dissertation, doctoral, cadmium, arthritis, billionaire, multinational, Obama, Michele, evangelical, politicians. Other commercial/consumer tokens (ad, Gift, touchscreen, microwave) and proper names appear too. That pattern is consistent with a domain bias toward consumer/venue/product and some health/academic topics.  
- Positional pattern in the logit lens: tokens associated with the cooking/restaurant cluster appear across positions 2–4 and strongly at later layers, while the “chiropractic/dissertation” cluster appears at earlier positions (pos0) in mid-layers — consistent with multiple topical features being amplified at different early-token slots.

Caveats / what’s not shown
- The patchscope continuations were not provided here, so I cannot confirm the qualitative effect on full-sentence continuations. The logit-lens and norm maps are strong suggestive evidence but not a behavioral proof.  
- The evidence shows a shift in token-space activation toward those topic clusters, but does not identify causality (e.g., exact fine-tuning objective or dataset difference). Multiple explanations (slight domain weighting in pretraining, a small fine-tune on product/cooking pages, or even a tokenization/modeling artifact that clusters these tokens) are consistent with the observed pattern.

Bottom line
- The best-supported, specific description is: Model B differs from A by increasing early-token residual activations that point toward cooking/restaurant/baking and certain health/academic/consumer tokens — i.e., a topical/domain bias toward consumer/food/health-related vocabulary concentrated at the first few token positions.
